intro: Patterns that consistently get better results from Codex — structured tasks, good context, and safe workflows.

items.title: Imperative, bounded tasks
items.body: Good: 'Fix the null pointer in createUser when email is undefined'. Bad: 'The createUser function has issues'. Specific tasks produce surgical edits.

items.title: Reference exact locations
items.body: Include file paths and function names. 'In src/api/users.ts, in the updateUser function, add a check that...' beats 'fix the update function'.

items.title: State what not to touch
items.body: Add 'Do not modify other files' or 'Only change src/api/posts.ts' to keep diffs minimal.

items.title: Write an AGENTS.md
items.body: Like CLAUDE.md for Claude Code, AGENTS.md gives Codex persistent project context — stack, commands, conventions, and what NOT to do.

items.title: Always work in a branch
items.body: git checkout -b codex/feature-name before any Codex task. If something goes wrong: git checkout . to reset.

items.title: Verify with git diff
items.body: After every Codex session: git diff to review what changed. Run npm test. Stage changes with git add -p to pick only the good parts.

items.title: Explore before implementing
items.body: Start with: 'What files handle authentication in this project?' Review Codex's understanding before asking it to change anything.

items.title: Order multi-file changes
items.body: For changes that span files, list them in dependency order: 'Make these changes in order: 1. Add type to types.ts 2. Update model 3. Update API route'

items.title: Use before/after examples
items.body: For style-sensitive tasks (like callback→async/await conversions), show one 'before' and one 'after' example before asking Codex to apply the pattern across files.
